transcript:
paul_support: Hey team, escalated ticket from ACME (T#38901) — customer says streaming calls are being billed as 5xx when their client aborts mid-stream. They sent a sample request-id: req_0a1b2c3d and a short trace. Can someone triage?

devon_engineer: ok. can you paste the gateway log + request headers and the sample response we see? rough log lines fine.

paul_support: pasted sample (sanitized):

```
REQUEST ID: req_0a1b2c3d
POST /v1/streams
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
         Transfer-Encoding: chunked
         User-Agent: acme-bot/2.1

Gateway log:
[2026-03-16T14:22:01Z] proxy: conn 10.0.4.23 -> runtime: upstream_status=-, reason=client_reset, bytes_sent=1024
[2026-03-16T14:22:01Z] router: response_code=502 metric:count.5xx++ trace=req_0a1b2c3d
```

They claim client closed immediately after the final chunk trailer; no upstream 5xx returned. Billing shows a 5xx increment.

mina_billing: cc billing — if this is a customer-initiated abort we generally don't bill 5xx. But we need a reproducible classification rule.

jen_sre: this smells like the EOF heuristic in gateway proxy. We have a rule: if connection tear down happens before a full body ACK we mark as gateway_error. Historically that flips billing. need to know whether proxy sees FIN vs RST.

devon_engineer: can you try a small repro? easy node snippet to simulate client sending final chunk and doing an immediate socket destroy:

```
const net = require('net');
const req = net.createConnection(4321,'proxy');
req.write('POST /v1/streams HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n');
req.write('4\r\ndata\r\n0\r\n\r\n');
// immediate abrupt close
req.destroy();
```

If that reproduces, gateway currently interprets as upstream failure and increments 5xx. 

paul_support: ran the snippet against staging proxy (stg-proxy-5) — repro is consistent. Trace stg_req_77f. The middleware logs show "client closed before response headers" and metric counter 5xx++. Repro attached: https://staging-traces/repro/stg_req_77f

devon_engineer: thanks. so two parts: 1) classification (should this be a 4xx/no-bill event) 2) whether kernel-level socket close type (FIN vs RST) is visible. I suspect our proxy treats client half-close before body flush as upstream error due to a conservative mapping: any mid-stream socket close => 502. That's the heuristic we need to relax.

mina_billing: for the live customer, do we have an immediate refund play? I'd avoid broad refunds until we fix classification for all similar cases. we can offer credit while we investigate.

jen_sre: short-term mitigation: add a filter that ignores socket-close events if we already sent final chunk trailer and bytes_sent > 0 and upstream_status is missing. that'll stop misclassifying graceful client aborts.

devon_engineer: agree. proposed fix in runtime: if last_write_includes_chunk_terminator == true && close_seen_within(3s) then classify as client_abort_not_5xx. I'll open PR with tests that simulate chunked client_destroy vs real 5xx. linking: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4521

paul_support: will relay workaround to ACME: ensure client waits ~3s after final chunk or set `X-Redwood-Client-Flush: true` header to tell gateway to treat early FIN as client-initiated abort. customer ok with temporary header.

devon_engineer: action items:
- devon: PR #4521 with tests + changelog (ETA 48h)
- jen: add dashboard filter for `label=client_abort_not_5xx` + backfill counts (ETA 24h)
- mina: propose one-off credit for T#38901 (I'll draft messaging) (ETA end of day)
- paul: reach back to customer with header workaround and ask for timeline

paul_support: noted. small follow-up: if anyone can sanity-check the proposed test harness I pushed to staging under /test/proxy/chunked-close that'd help. I saw a flake once where kernel delivered ECONNRESET vs EPIPE depending on load.

devon_engineer: will run the harness. if we see ECONNRESET -> still treat as client_abort if we previously observed final-chunk-trailer. otherwise fallback to current 5xx mapping.

mina_billing: thanks all. please add the customer credit SKU to the support ticket when you post the update.

paul_support: thanks. tagging @devon_engineer @jen_sre @mina_billing :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled for canary to include PR #4521 on staging-proxy-5 at 2026-03-17T02:00Z

paul_support: closing loop in the ticket after canary verification. will keep thread updated.
